title: capacity-drawdown-refill-scenarios-na-eu-apac-2026-q4
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a set of alternative operational scenarios for the next refilling and drawdown cycles of our GPU fleets across NA / EU / APAC (target window: Oct 2026 – Mar 2027). It's aimed at SRE + Fleet Planning + Partnerships to align procurement, cloud reservations, and burst reserve policies.

Summary (one-liner):
Plan A: conservative refill with long runway and smaller bursts;
Plan B: demand-driven refill with regional fast-buys;
Plan C: market-shock contingency (rapid refill + aggressive routing).

Assumptions used across scenarios:
- Baseline steady-state throughput demand = 1.0e9 token-ops / month (current observed avg over last 30 days)
- Average real RT50 latency target = 120ms for hosted tier, 80ms for dedicated customers
- Effective GPU capacity measured in "serving units" (SU) where 1 SU ≈ throughput of one A100-80GB under typical batching; heterogeneous fleet normalized to SU.
- Current fleet (2026-07-01 snapshot): NA=7,200 SU, EU=4,000 SU, APAC=2,400 SU (total 13,600 SU). Warm buffer target = 15% of regional peak.
- Decommission window for legacy instances (P4/RTX mix) starts Nov 2026; net SU removal = 1,500 SU globally if not replaced.

Key regional priorities (short):
- NA: primary growth market; keep 2-month reserve buffer; prefer cloud reservations with 12–24 month commitments for cost predictability.
- EU: constrained by procurement lead times and data residency; prefer Dedicated pool expansions and limited spot bursts.
- APAC: volatile demand spikes; rely on burst-on-demand and cross-region fallback into NA as last resort.

Scenario matrices (month-level cadence):
- Months: Oct 2026 | Nov 2026 | Dec 2026 | Jan 2027 | Feb 2027 | Mar 2027

Plan A — Conservative Refill (safe runway):
- Intention: prioritize cost and stability. Refill only to match measured growth + maintain 15% buffer. No aggressive fast-buys.
- Actions: enable 1x 12-month reservation purchase in NA (adds 800 SU in Oct); delay legacy decomm until Feb 2027 to spread risk.
- Forecast SU by region (end of month):
  NA: Oct 7600 | Nov 7600 | Dec 7700 | Jan 7600 | Feb 7600 | Mar 7600
  EU: Oct 4100 | Nov 4100 | Dec 4100 | Jan 4100 | Feb 4100 | Mar 4100
  APAC: Oct 2500 | Nov 2500 | Dec 2500 | Jan 2400 | Feb 2400 | Mar 2400
- Utilization target (system): 65–75% average.
- Risk: if demand grows >10% QoQ, we hit latency backpressure in NA.

Plan B — Demand-Driven Refill (responsive):
- Intention: scale closest to demand with fast regional buys and short reservations. Use spot/accelerator bursts and cross-region routing.
- Actions: schedule 2x short-term (3–6 month) adds across NA and APAC; enable automated fast-buy trigger when queued tokens > threshold T1; expedite EU Dedicated order for 500 SU in Dec.
- Forecast SU by region (end of month):
  NA: Oct 7800 | Nov 8200 | Dec 9000 | Jan 9200 | Feb 9400 | Mar 9600
  EU: Oct 4000 | Nov 4200 | Dec 4700 | Jan 4700 | Feb 4700 | Mar 4700
  APAC: Oct 2600 | Nov 3000 | Dec 3400 | Jan 3600 | Feb 3800 | Mar 4200
- Utilization target: keep p95 under 85% for NA and APAC.
- Risk: higher monthly cost; negotiation needed with cloud vendors to cap spot volatility.

Plan C — Market-Shock Contingency (aggressive refill + routing):
- Intention: defend SLAs during sudden demand shock (e.g., competitor launch, viral event). Mix of immediate cloud fast-buys + reserve preemption policies.
- Actions: pre-approved PO for 2K SU in NA available within 48h (finance hold ready), enable cross-region fallback policies and pre-warm VPN routes for Private customers. Execute legacy decommission early to reclaim some capacity after validation.
- Forecast (shock window Oct–Dec, then normalizing):
  NA: Oct 10000 | Nov 11000 | Dec 11000 | Jan 9200 | Feb 9000 | Mar 8800
  EU: Oct 4500 | Nov 5200 | Dec 5200 | Jan 4700 | Feb 4500 | Mar 4400
  APAC: Oct 3200 | Nov 3800 | Dec 4200 | Jan 4000 | Feb 3800 | Mar 3600
- Utilization target: accept short-term spikes to 90–95% while scaling.
- Risk: cost overruns and contractual consequences for aggressive short-term purchases.

Refill trigger matrix (operational thresholds):
- T1 (fast-buy 48h trigger): regional queued token load > 1.2x rolling 7d average AND p95 latency > target for 2 consecutive hours.
- T2 (priority refill, 7d): sustained utilization > 80% for 7d and customer-impacting errors > 1% of requests.
- T3 (emergency procurement): system-level saturated queues + incident declared.

Decommission / drawdown plan (legacy GPUs):
- Goal: reclaim 1,500 SU of older units with minimum customer impact.
- Process: schedule pilot decomm of 300 SU in Jan 2027 (APAC) -> monitor QoS -> stagger remaining decomm across Feb–Apr 2027.
- Rollback criteria: >5% latency regressions for >24h, or >3% error increase.

Cost heuristics (rough monthly delta estimates):
- Plan A incremental monthly cost vs baseline: +$120k for reservations + minor Opex smoothing.
- Plan B incremental monthly cost: +$250k–$420k depending on spot/fast-buy mix.
- Plan C worst-case monthly cost (shock): +$700k–$1.1M in short windows.

Operational runbook (first 90 days):
- Week 1: lock Plan choice (exec sign-off). Trigger pre-approvals with finance for planned buys.
- Week 2–4: implement T1/T2 telemetry hooks into Console (alerts, runbooks).
- Week 5–8: do a dry-run fast-buy and a cross-region fallback drill (SRE + on-call).
- Week 9–12: revisit reservations and finalize decommission cadence.

Open questions / notes to self:
- What is the expected contract lead time from vendor X for 1k SU in EU? (pinged procurement on 2026-07-06, awaiting reply)
- Need more granular per-model SU mapping (small Llama variants vs larger instruction-tuned models change SU equivalence). Marcus to produce mapping (JIRA INFRA-1024).
- Evaluate cost parity between 12-month reservations vs 3–6 month fast-buys for NA — finance wants scenarios by 2026-07-22.

Action items (owners):
- Asha: finalize Plan recommendation and run deck for leadership (due 2026-07-20).
- Marcus: produce model->SU conversion table + run simulation for Plan B (INFRA-1024) (due 2026-07-23).
- Rohit: validate EU procurement lead times and supply constraints (concrete vendor ETA) (due 2026-07-19).
- Elena: implement Console alerts for T1/T2 (due 2026-07-28).

Appendix — quick snapshot metrics (current baseline 2026-07-01):
- Total SU: 13,600; Warm buffer target (15%): 2,040 SU; Peak daily demand (last 30d): 11,900 SU observed; Current mean utilization: 72%.

- Capacity master (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFRA/Regional+Capacity+Master
- Open tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/issues/?jql=project%20%3D%20INFRA%20AND%20status%20in%20(Open%2C%20In%20Progress)%20ORDER%20BY%20priority

Notes: this is a working doc — numbers are estimates. Prefer conservative, documented moves where customer-facing SLAs could be impacted.
